examples.question_text:
The future value table gives the following factors for end-of-year contributions.
$\begin{array}{c|cc} n & 5\% & 6\% \\ \hline 4 & 4.3101 & 4.3746 \\ 5 & 5.5256 & 5.6371 \end{array}$
An investor deposits $\$1000$ at the end of each year for $5$ years at $6\%$ p.a. compounded annually. Use the table to calculate the future value and interest earned.
examples.solution_text:
Use row $n=5$ and column $r=6\%$: the future value factor is $5.6371$.
$\begin{aligned} FV &= 5.6371\times1000 \\ FV &= \$5637.10 \\ I &= 5637.10-(5\times1000) \\ I &= \$637.10 \end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
The future value table gives the following factors for end-of-period contributions.
$\begin{array}{c|cc} n & 2\% & 3\% \\ \hline 4 & 4.1216 & 4.1836 \\ 6 & 6.3081 & 6.4684 \end{array}$
An investor deposits $\$400$ at the end of each quarter for $1.5$ years at $8\%$ p.a. compounded quarterly. Use the table to calculate the future value and interest earned.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned} r &= \frac{8\%}{4}=2\% \\ n &= 1.5\times4=6 \end{aligned}$
Use row $6$ and column $2\%$: the future value factor is $6.3081$.
$\begin{aligned} FV &= 6.3081\times400 \\ FV &= \$2523.24 \\ I &= 2523.24-(6\times400) \\ I &= \$123.24 \end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
The present value table gives the following factors for end-of-year payments.
$\begin{array}{c|cc} n & 4\% & 6\% \\ \hline 2 & 1.89 & 1.83 \\ 3 & 2.78 & 2.67 \end{array}$
Find the single amount required now to provide payments of $\$3000$ at the end of each year for $3$ years, earning $4\%$ p.a. compounded annually. Use the supplied table.
examples.solution_text:
Use row $n=3$ and column $r=4\%$: the present value factor is $2.78$.
$\begin{aligned} PV &= 2.78\times3000 \\ PV &= \$8340 \end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
The tables give these factors for end-of-quarter contributions.
$\begin{array}{c|cc} & n & r=2\% \\ \hline \text{Present value factor} & 8 & 7.3255 \\ \text{Future value factor} & 8 & 8.5830 \end{array}$
An annuity receives $\$2000$ at the end of each quarter for $2$ years at $8\%$ p.a. compounded quarterly. Calculate its present and future values using the tables. Check that investing the present value now, with no further deposits or withdrawals, gives approximately the same future value. Give monetary answers to the nearest cent.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned} r &= \frac{8\%}{4}=2\% \\ n &= 2\times4=8 \\ PV &= 7.3255\times2000 \\ PV &= \$14\,651.00 \\ FV &= 8.5830\times2000 \\ FV &= \$17\,166.00 \end{aligned}$
Check the single investment over all $8$ quarters.
$\begin{aligned} FV &= 14651(1.02)^8 \\ FV &\approx \$17\,165.98 \end{aligned}$
The values differ by $\$0.02$ because the table factors are rounded.

examples.question_text:
The future value tables give these factors for end-of-period contributions.
$\begin{array}{c|cc} & n & \text{Rate per period} \\ \hline \text{Annual factor }5.6371 & 5 & 6\% \\ \text{Monthly factor }69.7700 & 60 & 0.5\% \end{array}$
Plan A deposits $\$2400$ at the end of each year for $5$ years at $6\%$ p.a. compounded annually. Plan B deposits $\$200$ at the end of each month for $5$ years at $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. Use the factors to find both future values and how much more interest Plan B earns.

The future value table gives these factors for end-of-year contributions.
$\begin{array}{c|cc} n & 3\% & 4\% \\ \hline 5 & 5.309 & 5.416 \\ 6 & 6.468 & 6.633 \end{array}$
An investor deposits $\$1000$ at the end of each year for $7$ years. Interest is $4\%$ p.a. compounded annually for the first $6$ years, then $5\%$ for Year $7$. Use the table to find the balance after the seventh deposit.
examples.solution_text:
Use the $6$-year factor at $4\%$, then apply the new rate before adding the seventh deposit.
$\begin{aligned} V_6 &= 6.633\times1000 \\ V_6 &= \$6633 \\ V_7 &= 6633(1.05)+1000 \\ V_7 &= \$7964.65 \end{aligned}$
